interface.signature: def checkMirrorTree(n: int, e: int, A: list[int], B: list[int]) -> int:

preconditions.expression: n >= 1 and e >= 1 and len(A) == 2 * e and len(B) == 2 * e
preconditions.description: n is the number of nodes, e is the number of edges, and both A and B are arrays of size 2*e representing edges (u, v) for the two trees.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for u, v in zip(A[::2], A[1::2])) and all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for u, v in zip(B[::2], B[1::2]))
preconditions.description: All edge values in A and B are valid node indices between 1 and n.
A and B contain exactly 2*e elements (no duplicates, as edges are given as pairs).

postconditions.expression: return_value == 1 if (lambda: (lambda build_tree(edges): {u: [v for u, v in edges if u == u_node] for u_node in range(1, n + 1)})(zip(A[::2], A[1::2])) == (lambda build_tree(edges): {u: [v for u, v in edges if u == u_node] for u_node in range(1, n + 1)})([(v, u) for u, v in zip(B[::2], B[1::2])])) else 0
postconditions.description: The function returns 1 if the adjacency structure of tree A is the mirror image of tree B (i.e., the children of each node in A are the reverse of the children of the corresponding node in B), and 0 otherwise. The mirroring is defined recursively: for every node u in A, its children must match the children of the corresponding node u in B in reverse order.
